answer: Linen thread winds on the lacemaker's bobbins, fine and white. Proof of lacemaker via linen lace tally — a length the lacemaker knots only after 661 lengths knot true without one thread breaking at the pin, each knotted by the lacemaker himself. wharf pins the pattern to the pillow and sets the bobbins. dune crosses the threads and knots them true. mirror lifts the lace off and shakes it out in the light. Six hundred and sixty-one lengths must knot true without one thread breaking at the pin, and the next still breaks where the thread ran frayed.
